findings.obligation: The shipped folded-rail promise owes the revealed word visible beside the strip. Making the rail position: sticky changes its stacking: a stacking context at z-index auto, painted below later positioned content such as .column and .issue-card. The design must state the stacking of the rail against the content column.
findings.remediation: Design owns: add to ADR-003 and architecture.md a decision that .sidebar carries an explicit z-index above the positioned content (and below the overlays at css:454, 856, 1363), with the reason. Require the revealed-word hit-test row to run in the folded geometry on a board page that holds cards, with the word overlapping a column. Update the css:1080-1083 comment premise.

observations.text: O1 INSPECTIVE: z-index band checked against the whole shipped stylesheet. Every z-index: 200 card-drag-ghost (css:454), 100 #kb-overlay-root (1363), 60 .lane-menu (1812), 50 .modal (856), 30 flyout and phone label (1149, 1603; inside the rail context), 2 .column.lane-dragging (1911). The rail at 20 sits above all positioned content with auto or 2, and below all overlays. Other positioned layers (.issue-card 544, .column 1743, grip 575) declare no z-index. The ADR names modal, kb overlay and ghost but not .lane-menu at 60; it is above 20 so the band holds, a naming gap only. Because .app-shell is a flex row, z-index also applies to the rail on the phone where it is static; the bar paints at 20 over content, harmless.

O2 INSPECTIVE: ADR-004 is faithful. It supersedes 003, states the stacking mechanism, rejects the descendant z-index, over-overlay and drop-sticky alternatives, makes L8 hit-test run on a board page with cards, records the band as a standing browser-row check, and carries the ADR-002 pointer (finding 1). Prior findings 1 and 2 are answered. Quint model not changed by this revision; not rerun.
